author: potuz
content:
Had some free time at the airport, here's a benchmark all in the same computer, 1.8M validators. From most naive two chunks implementations (that is not using the hashtree trick) to vectorized optimized. 

```
1.8M validators on an Apple M4 Pro (14 cores):

┌─────────────────────────────────┬───────────────┐
│            Benchmark            │ Time per root │
├─────────────────────────────────┼───────────────┤
│ Single list, pairwise, one core │ 1,510 ms      │
├─────────────────────────────────┼───────────────┤
│ Single list, pairwise, 14 cores │ 169 ms        │
├─────────────────────────────────┼───────────────┤
│ Single list, batched vectorized │ 104 ms        │
├─────────────────────────────────┼───────────────┤
│ Separate lists, sequential      │ 42 ms         │
├─────────────────────────────────┼───────────────┤
│ Separate lists, concurrent      │ 27.6 ms       │
└─────────────────────────────────┴───────────────┘
```
The fastest "single list" version is still 4 times slower than the separate list, but it is **also** using a trick we currently use that exploits the fact that there are exactly 8 fields in the validator structure. So the actual difference  on this machine would be from 170ms to 28ms.
